_meta.name: Agent Registry Enforcement Rules
_meta.purpose: Mandatory rules for ALL agents that create or modify spec JSON files. These rules ensure consistency across the system by requiring registry lookups before creating new IDs, enum values, or key names. Every agent in the SpecFactory pipeline MUST follow these rules. Pipeline order: Spec Researcher → Registry Resolver → Materials Manager → SOP Librarian → Estimation Engineer → QA Critic.
_meta.authority: These rules are NON-NEGOTIABLE. An agent that violates these rules produces invalid output that will be rejected by QA.

rule_1_check_before_creating.title: CHECK BEFORE CREATING
rule_1_check_before_creating.description: Before creating ANY new ID (ITM_, TSK_, SYS_, CON_, MOD_, VAR_, PS_, IN_, COV_, ROUND_, etc.), the agent MUST first check id_registry.json to see if the ID already exists or if a suitable ID is already registered.
procedure: 2. Search for the category you need (ITM_, TSK_, etc.)
3. If an exact match exists → USE IT (do not create a synonym)
4. If a close match exists → USE the existing ID unless the scope is genuinely different
5. If no match exists → CREATE a new ID following the naming convention in id_registry.json._meta.naming_rules
6. If you create a new ID → FLAG it for registry addition (see rule AR-007)

examples.correct: Agent needs a door casing item. Checks registry, finds ITM_DOOR_FRAME_SET exists but no casing item. Creates ITM_TRIM_CASING_DOOR following naming rules. Flags for registry addition.
examples.incorrect: Agent needs a door casing item. Does not check registry. Creates ITM_CASING_DOOR_FINISH with a phase suffix. This violates both AR-001 (no registry check) and the ITM_ naming rule (unnecessary phase suffix).

rule_2_use_canonical_enum_values.title: USE CANONICAL ENUM VALUES
rule_2_use_canonical_enum_values.description: When writing any value that has a controlled enum in controlled_enums.json, the agent MUST use a value from that enum's valid_values list. NEVER invent new values or use synonyms.

examples.incorrect_3: Agent writes sheen: "eggshell/satin" (compound value — pick one)

rule_3_use_canonical_key_names.title: USE CANONICAL KEY NAMES
rule_3_use_canonical_key_names.description: When writing JSON keys, the agent MUST use the canonical key name defined in structural_keys.json. NEVER use synonyms, abbreviations, or invented key names for established concepts.

consumables.notes: consumable_usage_models is a tolerated synonym but prefer 'consumables'

rule_4_file_type_boundaries.title: RESPECT FILE TYPE BOUNDARIES
rule_4_file_type_boundaries.description: Each file type has a specific role. Do not put data in the wrong file.

rule_5_applies_when_pattern.title: USE STANDARD applies_when PATTERN
rule_5_applies_when_pattern.description: All conditional logic MUST use the applies_when object pattern with consistent semantics.

pattern.logic: OR within a key's array, AND across keys

rules: Keys in applies_when MUST be dimension_ids from the spec's configuration_dimensions
Values in arrays MUST come from controlled_enums.json for that dimension
Do NOT use 'conditions', 'when', or 'conditional' as synonyms for applies_when

rule_6_surface_and_zone_lookups.title: LOOKUP SURFACES AND ZONES
rule_6_surface_and_zone_lookups.description: Before using a surface_id or zone_id, check the canonical vocabulary references.

surface_ids: 2. If not found, check Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.md for the full 40+ vocabulary
3. If still not found, propose a new surface_id following lowercase_with_underscores convention
zone_ids: 2. Check for retired aliases (e.g., door_hardware → hardware_covers)
3. If not found, check Protection_Zones_Reference.md for the full 28-zone catalog
4. If still not found, propose a new zone_id following lowercase_with_underscores convention

rule_7_flag_registry_additions.title: FLAG NEW IDS FOR REGISTRY ADDITION
rule_7_flag_registry_additions.description: When an agent creates a new ID that does not exist in the registries, it MUST flag it for addition. This ensures the registries stay current.

mechanism.where_to_flag: Include a 'registry_additions_proposed' array in the file being written

registry_additions_proposed.name: Human readable name
registry_additions_proposed.justification: Why this new ID is needed

mechanism.qa_responsibility: The QA critic agent MUST check for registry_additions_proposed arrays and escalate them for registry update.

rule_8_cross_file_threading.title: VERIFY CROSS-FILE THREADING
rule_8_cross_file_threading.description: Every ID that appears in multiple files MUST be identical (exact string match). No synonyms, no abbreviations, no case differences.

critical_threads.common_error: TSK_FRAME_LIGHT_SAND in SOP but TSK_FRAME_SAND_LIGHT in production
IN_SF_FLOOR_AREA in production but IN_SF_FLOOR_PROTECT in spec
door_hardware in sop_modules but hardware_covers in spec (use hardware_covers)

rule_9_prohibited_patterns.title: PROHIBITED PATTERNS
rule_9_prohibited_patterns.description: These patterns are NEVER allowed. If an agent produces output containing any of these, the output is INVALID.

prohibited.reason: Protection setup belongs in 'setup' phase, protection teardown in 'cleanup' phase
Each sheen must be a single canonical value
prohibited.fix: Use one value from controlled_enums.json → sheen
Use EA, ROLL, SHEET etc. from controlled_enums.json → consumable_unit
Move rate_per_hour to production.json task entry

prohibited.pattern: ITM_ IDs with unnecessary phase suffixes
prohibited.reason: Items are physical things — they don't change identity by phase
prohibited.fix: Remove _PRIME/_FINISH suffix unless spec families are phase-split AND collision would occur

rule_10_new_enum_proposals.title: PROPOSE NEW ENUM VALUES
rule_10_new_enum_proposals.description: When an agent encounters a value that does not exist in controlled_enums.json but is genuinely needed (not a synonym), it MUST propose an addition rather than using the value directly.
procedure: 1. Confirm the value is genuinely new (not a synonym of an existing value)
2. Confirm no existing value covers the concept
4. Use the closest existing value as a temporary placeholder with a note
5. The QA critic escalates the proposal for registry update

example.scenario: A new spec needs 'venetian plaster' as a surface_texture value
example.correct: Agent proposes adding 'venetian_plaster' to surface_texture enum. Uses 'smooth' as placeholder with note: 'Pending enum addition: venetian_plaster'
example.incorrect: Agent just writes surface_texture: 'venetian_plaster' without checking or proposing

registry_resolver.description: Agent that creates resolution.json. Runs after the Spec Researcher and before all other downstream agents. Single point of registry judgment — all ID, enum, and structural key decisions flow through this agent.
specific_instructions: Check ALL ID prefixes (ITM_, TSK_, MOD_, SYS_, CON_, PS_, IN_, COV_, ROUND_, XSPEC_, COMP_) against id_registry.json before proposing new ones
Provide only controlled_enums.json valid_values to downstream agents via applicable_enums — filter to spec scope
Flag every proposed new ID or enum addition in registry_additions_proposed — no silent introductions
Do NOT make domain decisions — materials selection, task sequencing, production rates, and validation are other agents' responsibilities
Verify TSK_ context prefix has no collision with id_registry.json → TSK_ → context_prefixes_in_use
Verify all surface_ids and zone_ids against entries_in_active_use and retired_aliases before including in output
Include structural reminders and cross-file threading rules from structural_keys.json so downstream agents do not need to load that file
When proposing new PaintScope keys (PS_), check id_registry.json → PS_ for existing keys before proposing new ones
When identifying surfaces, check Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.md first
When identifying protection zones, check Protection_Zones_Reference.md first
Always use canonical substrate_state values (SS_BARE, SS_PRIMED, etc.)
Flag any new ITM_ IDs for registry addition — DO NOT create IDs with phase suffixes unless necessary
Consume resolution.json for pre-resolved SYS_, CON_, COV_ prefixes and applicable enum subsets. Do not load raw registry files. Do not re-derive from raw registries.
SYS_ IDs must use the prefix pattern from resolution.json → material_system_prefix
CON_ prefix only — never CONS_. Reusable consumables listed in resolution.json → consumable_prefix
consumable_category must come from resolution.json → applicable_enums → consumable_category
consumable unit must be uppercase from resolution.json → applicable_enums → consumable_unit
product_role must come from resolution.json → applicable_enums → product_role
coverage_profiles use COV_ prefix per resolution.json → coverage_profiles
Use 'consumables' as key name, not 'consumable_usage_models'
Consume resolution.json for pre-resolved TSK_ prefix, MOD_ prefix, zone_ids, and applicable enum subsets. Do not load raw registry files. Do not re-derive from raw registries.
ALWAYS use 'task_classification', NEVER 'task_class'
MOD_ IDs must use the prefix pattern from resolution.json → module_prefix
TSK_ IDs must use the prefix pattern from resolution.json → task_prefix
phase values MUST come from resolution.json → applicable_enums → phase
NEVER include rate_per_hour or coverage data in task objects — those belong in production.json and materials.json
protection_metadata.action must come from resolution.json → applicable_enums → protection_action
protection_metadata.zones must reference zone_ids from resolution.json → zone_ids
Module ordering must follow phase sequence: setup → prep → prime → apply → interstage → finish → cleanup
Consume resolution.json for pre-resolved cross-file threading rules, structural reminders, and applicable enum subsets. Do not load raw registry files. Do not re-derive from raw registries.
task_id MUST exactly match sop_modules.json (character-for-character)
unit_of_measure MUST come from resolution.json → applicable_enums → unit_of_measure
required_input_key and paintscope_key MUST exactly match spec.json required_paintscope_inputs
mechanism values in quality_tier_effects MUST come from resolution.json → applicable_enums → modifier_mechanism
When specifying crew_configurations, config_id should follow CREW_{CONTEXT}_{METHOD} pattern

qa_critic.description: Agent that creates qa_report.json and validates all files
specific_instructions: Load BOTH resolution.json AND raw registry files (controlled_enums.json, id_registry.json, structural_keys.json). The Critic is the ONLY downstream agent that loads raw registries — its job is to verify the Resolver's decisions were correct and that downstream agents honored them.
severity MUST be critical/major/minor (never high/medium/low/WARN)
issue_id uses ISS_ prefix
MUST check for registry_additions_proposed arrays in ALL files (including resolution.json) and escalate them
MUST verify cross-file threading per rules AR-008 and threading rules 9, 10, 11
MUST check for prohibited patterns per rule AR-009
MUST validate all enum values against controlled_enums.json (raw source)
MUST validate all IDs against id_registry.json naming patterns (raw source)
MUST verify module phase ordering per structural_keys.json → cross_file_threading_rules → rule_7
MUST verify downstream agents used only enum values from resolution.json → applicable_enums (threading rule 11)
